analysis:
The only changed hunk in MultiModelBatchSchedulerEngine.swift is at head lines 833-835: the call into prompt preparation now passes `promptCacheScope: cacheEnabled ? requestCacheScope : nil`. The comment says token reuse is partitioned like the prefix KV cache. The supplied units are base text at lines 1018-1606 and head text at lines 1-528. The changed lines (~833) lie outside both supplied excerpts, so I could not read the call site or the callee that consumes `promptCacheScope`. Base lines 1018-1606 are unchanged in this PR; I reviewed them only as surrounding context (native MiMo media path, makeEventStream, tokenizer utilities), and I saw no new behavior there.

Security direction: the change scopes a prompt/token-level reuse cache by the authenticated coordinator cache scope (the `cacheScope` stored property at head line 104, set only via the coordinator init). The scope is nil when `cacheEnabled` is false, which is the legacy or malformed coordinator case. This matches the T-041 posture: coordinator-authored scope, with callers unable to choose it. If anything it narrows cross-tenant sharing and does not add a regression I can see.

Unverified contracts and open questions for integration:
1. How the callee (the prompt-preparation pipeline taking `promptCacheScope`) treats a nil scope. It must not fall back to a shared global token-reuse cache across accounts. This is a possible cross-tenant TTFT or reuse channel (T-041 / SEC-035), but no evidence of it is supplied.
2. Whether the diffusion `requestCacheScope` fallback to `nativeLocalCacheScope` (head lines 442-443) is appropriate for the token cache. Remote requests do not use that fallback because `cacheScope` is non-empty.
3. Whether this new token-reuse cache is within the T-041 documented at-rest and in-memory surface (TTL, bounds, no at-rest storage). The threat model may need an update if it persists anything or adds a timing oracle.
No finding is reported because the callee is not visible.
